split_note: Split from BANK_GSIB per the interest-researcher's own confirmed finding: the merged treatment fails under stress. This actor represents the US-chartered G-SIB complex specifically, distinguished by a self-protective, jurisdiction-first resolution posture.
horizon_driver: Quarterly earnings and annual CCAR stress tests set the normal cadence, but the home resolution authority (FDIC) can act within days once stress is acute -- SVB was seized and resolved inside days in March 2023.

constraints.source: The US FDIC's Mar 2023 systemic-risk exception for SVB/Signature covered only US-chartered uninsured deposits, funded by a special assessment on US banks -- no cross-border, group-wide guarantee was extended (BIS FSI Executive Summary, 2023).
constraints.breaks_under: never observed to break -- this is the defining structural feature of the US resolution regime, not a negotiable constraint

constraints.source: The US maintained standard absolute-priority treatment in 2023 even as Switzerland inverted its own hierarchy; the Bank of England and ECB publicly aligned with the US/standard approach within days of the Swiss move (BoE statement, 20 Mar 2023).
constraints.breaks_under: acute national solvency crisis judged severe enough that FDIC/Treasury deviate from statutory priority -- no historical instance

stated_vs_revealed.stated: US G-SIBs operate under a harmonised, FSB/Basel-coordinated global resolution framework implying consistent treatment regardless of jurisdiction.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: The US ring-fenced its Mar 2023 systemic-risk-exception deposit guarantee to US-chartered deposits only, funded entirely domestically -- no extension to foreign branches or a shared international facility.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Confirms self-protective, jurisdiction-first behavior under stress, not global solidarity.

tripwires.if: a US G-SIB faces an acute solvency or deposit-run event
tripwires.then: expect a fast, domestically-funded, jurisdiction-limited resolution (FDIC systemic-risk exception pattern) with no automatic extension to non-US operations or counterparties

what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence of a binding, tested cross-border backstop commitment from a post-2023 Basel/FSB process would raise confidence in more internationally cooperative behavior.
